data.one_liner: A responsive Flutter navigation bar that switches between a full bar and a drawer based on screen size.
data.what_it_does: The package provides an AdaptiveNavBar widget that renders a traditional app bar on larger screens and collapses into a drawer menu on mobile devices. It relies on the material_ui library for theming and widget implementations.
use_when: You need a single navigation widget that works across web, desktop, and mobile without writing custom responsive code.
Your app already uses material_ui and targets Flutter 3.47+.
avoid_when: Your project still depends on the default flutter/material.dart library.
You require advanced navigation features like deep linking or nested routing beyond a simple bar.
strengths: Zero‑code responsive behavior – the widget adapts automatically.
Integrates with material_ui, keeping styling consistent.
Simple API – same as previous 1.x versions.
weaknesses: Requires migration to material_ui and Flutter 3.47+, which may be a breaking change for existing apps.
Limited to basic navigation UI; no built‑in routing or state management.
data.setup_notes: Add adaptive_navbar ^2.0.0 and material_ui to pubspec, ensure Flutter 3.47+ and migrate imports to material_ui (run dart fix --apply --code=migrate_design_widgets).

alternatives.name: responsive_framework
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a full set of breakpoints and responsive utilities to build custom navigation bars without a dedicated widget.

alternatives.name: responsive_builder
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers responsive widget builders that let you create your own adaptive navbar with fine‑grained control.

alternatives.name: value_layout_builder
alternatives.why_pick_it: A lightweight helper for building layout‑aware widgets, suitable for custom navbar implementations.
